rulings.challenge_claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that 11:30 shares no wording with 11:31 is byte-false, and the row's only Hebrew quotation is unpointed/unlabeled as skeleton tier.
rulings.grounds: Byte re-derivation (verse_map_oshb.json, spliced not retyped): Prov.11.30 and Prov.11.31 share the byte-identical accented token צַ֭דִּיק (righteous) -- exact match down to the cantillation mark, confirmed by direct token-set intersection between the two verses. The row's rejected_alternative sentence ('shares no wording with this verse's a-fortiori repayment argument') is therefore byte-false, not merely undisclosed. LF's own support review independently names this same token ('the only token 11:31 shares with 11:30 is the ubiquitous tsaddiq') yet filed 'support' without flagging that the row's own text asserts zero shared wording -- LF's cited evidence corroborates OL's challenge rather than contradicting it. Re-collated the row's own quote via collate.py --json (byte tier is the only quotation-grade tier for pointed text): result tier=skeleton, status GREEN but not byte -- the quote is unpointed, matching OL's claim. OBJECT-not-DIGIT check on OL's own supporting count: independently reswept book-wide occurrences of this exact word-form at four tiers (never through a shell, to avoid the accent-loss hazard) -- byte-identical accented token (this exact cantillation): 12 verses; accent-stripped word-bound (any cantillation, same vowels): 31; skeleton word-bound (singular form only): 34; skeleton contiguous substring (root, any inflection): 66. OL's cited '~66' (skeleton) matches exactly; OL's cited '17' does not match any of these four tiers and appears to be an inexact supporting digit -- this does not change the core finding, which rests on the exact-token intersection, not the book-wide count.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite rejected_alternative to disclose and downweight the shared tsadiq token as ordinary collection-wide vocabulary -- the same move already used successfully in this cluster's own P06-005/P06-007 rows for their shared resha'im term -- rather than asserting zero shared wording. Separately, replace the unpointed quote with the fully pointed bytes spliced from verse_map_oshb.json (oshb:Prov.11.31) or explicitly label the existing quote 'skeleton tier.' Test: re-run collate.py on the corrected quote and confirm tier=byte; confirm the corrected rejected_alternative no longer claims zero shared wording where a token-intersection check is positive.

rulings.grounds: Byte re-derivation (verse_map_oshb.json): oshb:Prov.12.2 (the verse actually BEFORE 12:3) reads 'tov yafiq ratson me-YHWH ve-ish mezimmot yarshia' -- favor-from-Yahweh and a wicked man's mezimmot (schemes/plans), no 'counsel' (etsah) content. oshb:Prov.12.4 (the verse actually AFTER 12:3) carries the crown/rot imagery (eshet chayil ateret ba'alah / u-kh'raqav be-atsmotav). Both clauses of the rejected_alternative are confirmed wrong on both direction and content. This is a convergence row with OL (below); the two challenges are DISTINCT defects -- LF's is a content/direction-accuracy error in the row's own auxiliary field, OL's is a citation-engagement gap -- not the same defect.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite rejected_alternative to correctly name 12:4 as the verse AFTER 12:3 (crown/rot imagery) and either drop the fabricated 'counsel verse after it' clause entirely or correctly attribute 12:2 (favor/wicked-mezimmot content, not counsel) as the verse BEFORE. rulings.challenge_claim: The B-colon's opening waw at 12:13 is mislabeled -- a vav-consecutive (wayyiqtol) verb form, not the simple conjunctive waw the row's own device_notes equates it with across the cluster -- and the claim that 12:14 'lacks an adversative waw altogether' is byte-false.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived the waw morphology from the pointed bytes before ruling (per assignment instruction), rather than trusting either packet's grammar claim. The 12:13 B-colon opener וַיֵּצֵ֖א is vav + patach + dagesh-forte-in-the-next-consonant + tsere -- the diagnostic wayyiqtol/vav-consecutive shape on a finite prefix-conjugation verb. By contrast the B-colon openers cited across this cluster's sibling rows are all simple conjunctive waw on a NON-finite head, with no possible consecution: 12:3 וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ (vav+shva on the noun 'root'), 12:6 וּפִ֥י (vav+shuruq, the regular pointing before a labial, on the noun 'mouth-of'), 12:7 וּבֵ֖ית (vav+shuruq before a labial, on the noun 'house-of'), 12:15 וְשֹׁמֵ֖עַ (vav+shva on the participle 'hearing'), 12:16 וְכֹסֶ֖ה (vav+shva on the participle 'concealing'). P06-013's own observed_substrate_signals text ('the B-colon's opening waw carries the adversative turn') applies the identical 'adversative waw' framing to this genuinely different construction -- UPHELD: this is a real, well-grounded grammatical conflation, structurally significant because the same unexamined label recurs across five-plus rows in this cluster. On the second sub-claim: 12:14's B-colon opener וּגְמ֥וּל is confirmed waw-prefixed -- a waw IS present, so a literal 'has no waw at all' reading is byte-false as OL states. But the row's actual phrase is 'lacks an adversative waw altogether,' which most naturally parses as 'lacks the adversative FORCE of a waw' (the whole phrase 'an adversative waw' as the missing object), not 'lacks any waw whatsoever' -- and under that reading the claim holds: the waw is present but non-adversative/continuative, since 12:14 is a synonymous rather than antithetic couplet (LF's own review reaches the identical grammatical conclusion: 'its own waw (u-gmul) is non-adversative since 12:14 is synthetic rather than antithetic'). REFINED: this sub-claim is a real but narrower defect -- ambiguous phrasing that risks a false reading -- not the clean byte-falsehood OL frames it as; it should not carry the same weight as the morphology-conflation finding.
rulings.remedy: (1) Split the 'adversative waw' label at 12:13 into an explicit vav-consecutive/wayyiqtol tag, distinct from the simple-conjunctive tag correctly used at 12:3/12:6/12:7/12:15/12:16 -- do not fold both under one gloss in device_notes or observed_substrate_signals. (2) Reword the 12:14 rejected_alternative clause from the ambiguous 'lacks an adversative waw altogether' to an unambiguous statement, e.g.: a waw is present but its force is continuative rather than adversative, because 12:14 is a synonymous, not antithetic, couplet. Test (the test that must be passed): re-derive every B-colon opener's pointed bytes in this construction-run and confirm the vav-consecutive tag is applied ONLY where a patach-vocalized, dagesh-forte-bearing waw precedes a finite prefix-conjugation verb; confirm the reworded 12:14 sentence affirms waw-presence rather than negating it.
